answer: Escrowed Reputation Drawdown. Each new identity must post a velvet escrow that decays only through verified economic activity, and every counterparty sees the remaining balance as a beacon of trustworthiness. Cloning raises total escrow linearly, so an attacker's capital cost scales with identity count while each clone earns only the reputation of its small initial balance. Like shrubs on a knoll, extra identities stand exposed and underfunded, forcing sustained locking costs per fake agent.
